clue.text: Watches labourites consuming fish

indicators.note: a thing consuming another swallows it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: left-wing Labour supporters are loosely called Reds
the gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: Someone observes Labour Party members tucking into a fish supper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watches' looks like a noun for timepieces but is a verb; 'labourites' stands for left-wingers in general.
explanation.definitionFit: To regard something is to look at it attentively, so regards is a verb synonym for observes.

clue.text: It's subject to ups and downs

definitions.text: It's subject to ups and downs

parts.words: It's subject to ups and downs
parts.note: the phrase usually describes a life of mixed fortunes, but here it is literal: a machine carrying people between floors

explanation.surface: Something leads an unsettled, up-and-down existence.
explanation.definitionFit: A lift, called this in American English, spends its working day rising and falling between floors.

clue.text: A peasant suffering breakage of foot

indicators.note: letters that suffer breakage are smashed and reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A farm labourer has broken a bone in the foot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffering breakage' rearranges A PEASANT. 'Foot' is not the body part but the unit of verse rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody a metrical foot of two short syllables then one long one is called an anapaest.

clue.text: Is girl in seedy bar perfunctory?

indicators.note: the word in shows one piece sitting within the other

parts.note: a dive is a disreputable drinking den
taken as written
Miss is a title for a young woman

explanation.surface: A question about whether a young woman in a dodgy bar is offhand.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'dive' is informal for a shabby bar or club.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfunctory or dismissive response is offhand, showing little interest or care.

clue.text: Colorado firm used by Chanel

parts.note: CO is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Colorado
Co is short for company, a business firm

explanation.surface: A company in Colorado is supplying the Chanel fashion house.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is oblique: Coco was the name the designer Gabrielle Chanel went by.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabrielle Chanel, the French couturier, was known by the nickname Coco.

clue.text: Commandos' leader soon to impound new gun

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter
to impound something is to shut it in, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: anon is an old word for soon

explanation.surface: A commando chief is about to seize a newly made weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to impound' puts N inside ANON to give ANNON, after C from 'Commandos' leader'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannon is a large heavy piece of artillery, a kind of gun.

clue.text: Greek fellow's getting excellent return from capital

parts.note: Nicos is a common Greek man's name, the apostrophe-s supplying its final letter

indicators.note: a return comes back, so the letters for excellent are read backwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written here as AI

explanation.surface: A Greek man earns an excellent profit from his investment capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns AI (A1, excellent) into IA. 'capital' looks financial but means a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicosia is the capital city of Cyprus.

clue.text: Godly man and I ran off before being smothered

parts.note: ST is short for saint, a holy person
fled means ran away

explanation.surface: A holy man and the speaker fled the scene shortly before being smothered.
explanation.definitionFit: To stifle is to suffocate, so stifled means suffocated, like being smothered.

clue.text: Sadly solitary opponent of the Commonwealth

indicators.note: the adverb tells us the letters come out badly arranged and must be put in a new order

explanation.surface: A lonely figure stands against the Commonwealth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' rearranges SOLITARY. The Commonwealth here is Cromwell's republic of 1649 to 1660, not the modern association of nations.
explanation.definitionFit: Supporters of the Crown opposed Cromwell's republican Commonwealth, so a Cavalier was its opponent.

clue.text: A leper's dire deterioration

indicators.note: dire means dreadful, telling us the letters are in a terrible state and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A sufferer from leprosy is getting worse at an alarming rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dire' rearranges A LEPERS; here the apostrophe-s of leper's does supply a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A relapse is a falling back into illness after apparent recovery, a worsening.

clue.text: Complain angrily when the radio's kaput

definitions.meaning: to vent opinions loudly and indignantly
a broken radio gives no audio: its volume is gone, read literally as two words

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles loudly because the wireless has broken down.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to rant, while read literally it describes a set that has gone silent.

clue.text: Artist's accessory used by ambulancemen

definitions.meaning: a painter's canvas is pulled taut over a wooden frame of this name
paramedics carry patients on a portable bed of this name

explanation.surface: An item that serves both a painter and paramedics.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are things that extend: a frame tensioning canvas and a litter for carrying the injured.

clue.text: I am sadly upset by such fare

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns over, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
alas is an exclamation said sadly

explanation.surface: Someone is distressed by the food on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses the whole of IM + ALAS, IMALAS, read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a spicy cured sausage, a kind of food or fare.

clue.text: Mineral extracted from London waterway

definitions.meaning: a green mottled rock-forming silicate mineral has this name
the lake in Hyde Park, London, bears this name

explanation.surface: A mineral is being mined from a lake in the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The rock gets its name from its snake-like markings, and the curving Hyde Park lake from its snaking shape.

clue.text: Humorist wants to draw leader out

indicators.note: out means not in proper order, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A comic writer wants to sketch the party leader.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges DRAW LEADER. The Victorian writer of nonsense verse was also an artist, so 'draw' fits the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victorian author of The Owl and the Pussy-cat was a famous writer of nonsense verse and limericks.

clue.text: Small houses require small beds

definitions.meaning: a cot is an old or poetic word for a cottage
a cot is a child's bed with high sides

explanation.surface: Tiny homes need little beds.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a humble dwelling, the other a baby's crib.

clue.text: Two urban areas with educational links

definitions.text: Two urban areas with educational links

parts.words: Two urban areas with educational links
parts.note: sounds like university cities, but means places in different countries paired officially, often arranging school exchanges

explanation.surface: A pair of cities share connections in education.
explanation.definitionFit: Paired communities in different countries maintain civic and cultural ties, including exchange visits for schoolchildren.

clue.text: Principal warder initially displayed some bottle

indicators.note: says the second word, for the warder, is shown first, ahead of the word for principal

parts.note: screw is prison slang for a warder
top means chief or principal

explanation.surface: A senior prison officer showed some courage early on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some bottle' suggests the British slang for courage, but it means a type of bottle; 'initially displayed' says the warder's word comes first, and screw is British prison slang for a guard.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottle sealed with a threaded cap rather than a cork is one type of bottle.

clue.text: Supports a bishop inside quarters

indicators.note: inside places one piece within the other

parts.note: backs means supports
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: Someone backs a bishop who is housed somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Right Reverend, abbreviated RR, is the formal style of an Anglican bishop, a convention a solver may not know.
explanation.definitionFit: Barracks are buildings housing soldiers, their living accommodation.

clue.text: Parent conceals pork-pie from eastern sage

indicators.note: a thing that conceals another holds it hidden within

parts.note: mama is a word for mother
a pork-pie is a flat-crowned hat

explanation.surface: A mother hides a pork pie from an Indian holy man.
explanation.walkthrough: A pork-pie is not food here but a style of hat with a flat round crown.
explanation.definitionFit: In India a mahatma is a revered wise man, the title famously given to Gandhi.

clue.text: Coiffeur uses pen to keep a record

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs
to list things is to record them

explanation.surface: A hairdresser writes appointments down with a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like a writing tool, but it is an enclosure for pigs.
explanation.definitionFit: A hair stylist and a coiffeur are both hairdressers.

clue.text: He appears in church with retired secretary

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: PA is a personal assistant

explanation.surface: A man turns up at church with his former secretary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' reverses PA to AP.
explanation.definitionFit: A chap is a man, informally, so the pronoun can stand for it.

clue.text: Combined to make singer win the lady

parts.note: an alto is a singer in the low female or high male range
to get a prize is to win it
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A singer combines his voice with others to win over a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Altogether means all in all, in total, as when sums are combined.

clue.text: Opening a superior item from the patisserie

parts.note: a gate is an opening in a fence
U is the label for upper-class usage, hence superior

explanation.surface: A grand cake is on show at the opening of a smart bakery.
explanation.walkthrough: U meaning upper-class or superior is a British convention from the 1950s 'U and non-U' debate.
explanation.definitionFit: A gateau is a rich cream cake sold in French pastry shops.

clue.text: Gloomy auditor in arid surroundings

indicators.note: arid's surroundings means the word for arid goes round the other piece

parts.note: dry means arid
an ear is the organ that hears, a listener

explanation.surface: A depressing account inspector is working in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'auditor' looks financial but means something that hears; 'surroundings' says the word for arid goes round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreary means dismal and depressing, like gloomy.

clue.text: A good lot of youngsters are glowing

parts.note: a litter is a group of young animals born together

explanation.surface: A large group of children have bright, shining faces.
explanation.definitionFit: Aglitter means sparkling, shining with light, as when glowing.

clue.text: They say he'll succeed with Jane

indicators.note: they say signals that the word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: an heir will succeed to a title or estate

explanation.surface: People predict a man will do well with a woman named Jane.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition completes a title: Jane Eyre is the novel by Charlotte Bronte.
explanation.definitionFit: Charlotte Bronte's heroine is a governess named Jane, so the surname goes with her first name.

clue.text: Reportedly permitted us to serve vegetable

indicators.note: reportedly signals that what follows is heard, not read

parts.note: let us means allowed us

explanation.surface: We were allowed to serve greens.
explanation.definitionFit: Lettuce is a leafy green salad plant.

clue.text: Assemble by crusader port to commit slaughter

parts.note: to mass is to gather together
Acre, in present-day Israel, was a key port of the Crusaders

explanation.surface: Knights gather beside a port taken in the Crusades to kill many.
explanation.walkthrough: Acre is the historic port in northern Israel, captured and held by the Crusaders.
explanation.definitionFit: To massacre is to kill large numbers indiscriminately, to butcher.

clue.text: Offer to publish work written in plain language

indicators.note: written in means one piece is entered within the other

parts.note: prose is ordinary written language, not verse
op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: Someone offers to publish a piece composed in plain style.
explanation.walkthrough: Op (opus) is a convention for a work, as in musical catalogue numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: To propose is to put forward for consideration, as with a motion put up for debate.
